This is the first thing they need and it used to be a grey italic line at the very bottom of the page, under the whole brief - so the answer to "where do I write this?" sat below the thing it was needed for. `repo_url` is the cohort org's repo list filtered to this assignment rather than one student's address: the page is public and identical for everyone, and GitHub shows a signed-in student only the repos they can see, so the filter lands on their own. Absent while the assignment is pending - there is nothing at the other end of it yet. {%- endcomment -%} {%- comment -%} `submit_via` (site.py, off the assignment's own grading_config.yml) is the SHAPE: `external` is handed in off GitHub - Moodle, Kaggle, in class - and NO repo is created for it at all. So there is nothing to open and nothing to name: the brief below says where the work goes, and `submit_url` puts a button on it when the assignment names an address. This block used to print off `repo_url` alone, so a Moodle assignment told the whole cohort that a push to `main` was its submission. `escape`: `repo_name` is a SHAPE, `-`, and those angle brackets make `` an unknown HTML tag that the browser silently drops - so the name rendered as `assignment-1-` with the useful half missing. `data-dsl-repo`: the repo SHAPE, and the one thing on the page that a reader with a profile can be told exactly. open_in.html rewrites every one of these to the real name (`assignment-1-jane`) and repoints every `data-dsl-repo-url` beside them at that repo, so a student stops reading `` and substituting themselves. Marked rather than matched on the prose, because the sentences around them are reworded. {%- endcomment -%} {% if page.submit_via == "external" or page.repo_url %}
